text:
ara: Quick sync — I'm proposing a "customer-managed throttle handshake" for Private/VPC: customers can author per-org / per-api-key rate caps and burst quotas, we push an enforcement contract into their data plane. Need alignment on enforcement model and failure modes.

sam: +1 to customer-managed policy, but we need a safe default if they misconfigure. Suggest three modes: passive (telemetry-only), advisory (enforce but with soft-logs), strict (hard reject).

mei: agree on modes. Implementation idea: a signed policy blob that the control plane verifies and then the sidecar (customer-owned) enforces. That lets us audit integrity without owning enforcement runtime.

julian: question — for Private deployments we sometimes don't have a reachable control plane. How do we handle split-brain & drift? If sidecar has stale policy it could under/over throttle.

ara: good point. proposal: embed policy version + expiry + monotonic sequence. Sidecars should fall back to last-known-good and emit a "policy_stale" metric. If expiry reached -> fallback to conservative default (lower of customer policy and vendor-safe baseline).

sam: example policy (sketch):
```json
{
  "version": "v1",
  "org_id": "org-123",
  "rules": [
    {"target": "api_key:abc", "rate_per_min": 6000, "burst": 1500},
    {"target": "org:org-123", "rate_per_min": 20000, "burst": 5000}
  ],
  "enforcement": "strict",
  "expires_at": "2026-06-01T00:00:00Z",
  "signature": "..."
}
```

mei: thumbs up. Also include a "fallback_action" field: drop, queue, or degrade (route to cheaper model). That last one is powerful for keeping SLAs with graceful degradation.

julian: telemetry implications — need per-sidecar counters for allowed, blocked, queued, degraded, plus histograms for burst sizes. Also track "policy_apply_latency" so we know how long it takes to roll a change across nodes.

ara: UX: console should expose a preview that shows projected QPS after rule change (simulate over last 24h). We can do this by replaying recent telemetry against the new policy in a dry-run mode. @tamara can the Console team support a dry-run simulation endpoint?

tamara: yep we can. We'll need the policy schema stabilized and a small job to replay aggregated windowed metrics (not raw logs) to keep costs down. We can show a confidence band. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

sam: security note — signature verification must use customer or vendor key? If customer-managed, they might want keys in their KMS. For private/on-prem we should support customer-supplied public keys. For hosted dedicated we can host signing but allow rotation.

mei: agree. support two modes: customer-signed (preferred) and vendor-signed with hosted key (for simple self-serve). Document key rotation procedures.

julian: rollout plan idea: 1) implement passive mode + telemetry + stale policy metric; 2) enable advisory with logs and console preview; 3) enable strict enforcement in canary group (10 tenants) with alerting. Also add an emergency override endpoint for SRE.

ara: good. Who owns canary infra? ops-bot: created ticket INF-5632 to track canary infra & SLOs.

ops-bot: INF-5632: "VPC customer throttle handshake canary" created and assigned to eng-platform. Priority: P2.

sam: also need to define API for policy submission: POST /v1/policies with body=policy-blob, validate+sign flow, response includes "applied_version" and diff. Let's write an API contract doc.

mei: I'll draft the API contract and the sidecar shim. Will push a RFC by EOD tomorrow.

ara: action items: mei draft RFC, tamara prototype dry-run simulation, julian define telemetry & alerting signals, sam write API contract stub. We'll meet Friday for final alignment.

tamara: I'll add a Console ticket and wire a preview prototype to the dev console.

julian: note — metrics to add: policy_stale_count, policy_applied_count, throttle_block_count, throttle_degraded_count, burst_utilization_p95. We'll want these in New Relic & our internal dashboards.

ara: thanks all. If no objections I'll start the RFC tonight. :thumbsup:

sam: no objections. excited to see the draft.

mei: +1

julian: +1
